en.title: Bipartition Cost of a Tree
en.description:
Given a tree in which each node has a positive integer value. Divide the nodes into as few non-empty groups as possible such that no group contains adjacent nodes. The cost of a group is its maximum value minus its minimum value. Output the sum of the costs of all groups. With only one node, there is a single group with cost 0.

The input format, examples, and test data are compiled and written by CSWork.
en.input: The first line contains n (1..100000); the second line contains n values (1..10⁹); then n−1 lines with edges u v, where nodes are numbered 1..n. The input is guaranteed to be a tree.
en.output: Output the answer as described; multiple results are separated by spaces, in order.
en.explanation: The example inputs and outputs follow the rules above directly; see the solution for the full algorithm.
hints: Color the tree black and white with an iterative traversal, and maintain the minimum and maximum of each of the two colors.
